description: Curated technical facts and must-cover checklists for local interview coaching. Not evidence of personal work.

entries.title: Selenium implicit and explicit waits
entries.facts: Implicit wait is a WebDriver session timeout applied when finding elements (findElement/findElements), not a browser-level setting and not a wait for every page element or arbitrary condition. Explicit wait via WebDriverWait polls a specified condition (e.g. visibilityOfElementLocated or elementToBeClickable) until satisfied or timeout. Prefer explicit waits for dynamic UI and avoid mixing the two because compounded timeout behavior can be confusing.
must_cover: Implicit: session-wide timeout for locating elements
Prefer explicit for dynamic UI; avoid mixing waits

entries.title: Flaky automation tests
entries.facts: Flaky tests intermittently pass or fail without a relevant application change. Reproduce and inspect logs, screenshots, synchronization, locator stability, shared data, environment, timing and parallel execution. Fix root causes with condition-based explicit waits, reliable locators, isolated data and cleanup. Retries can be temporary diagnostics or containment, not the primary fix; track recurring failure trends.
must_cover: Diagnose using logs and reproduce failures
Fix synchronization, locators, data or environment root causes
Retries are temporary, not a substitute for a fix

entries.title: REST Assured API automation framework
entries.facts: A maintainable REST Assured API test framework can use Java 11, Maven, TestNG, reusable request/response specifications, configuration, authentication helpers, payload builders, API clients, assertions and optional JSON schema validation. Allure can generate reports and CI/CD can execute suites. These are possible components, not proof they were all implemented. If a CV establishes TestNG, name TestNG for that candidate rather than saying TestNG or JUnit.
must_cover: Modular request specification and test structure
Assertions, reporting and CI/CD when supported by CV

entries.title: TestNG testing framework
entries.facts: TestNG supports annotations such as @BeforeMethod and @Test, groups, priorities, dependencies, data-driven tests via @DataProvider, and parallel execution. Avoid depending on test order where possible. Maven Surefire can run suites and CI can publish reports.

entries.title: Cucumber BDD
entries.facts: Cucumber uses Gherkin Given/When/Then scenarios mapped to step definitions. Keep scenarios business-readable, reusable and independent; Page Objects or API clients hold implementation details. BDD is collaboration around examples, not just a test automation tool.

entries.title: Page Object Model and Selenium
entries.facts: Page Object Model encapsulates page locators and interactions, separating UI implementation from test assertions and flows. Use explicit waits for relevant conditions, stable locators, and avoid exposing low-level WebElements unnecessarily. PageFactory is optional and not required for POM.

entries.title: Java collections
entries.facts: ArrayList is a resizable array implementation of List. TreeMap sorts keys; LinkedHashMap maintains insertion order by default. Use the dedicated HashMap versus ConcurrentHashMap reference for thread safety and null differences.

entries.title: Java 8+ streams and Optional
entries.facts: Streams support declarative map/filter/reduce operations; intermediate operations are lazy until a terminal operation. Optional represents an optional result, not a replacement for every null. Avoid side effects in stream pipelines, particularly parallel streams.

entries.title: Java OOP
entries.facts: Encapsulation hides state behind methods; abstraction exposes essential behavior; inheritance models is-a relationships; polymorphism lets one interface dispatch different implementations. Favor composition over inheritance when relationships are not genuinely is-a.

entries.title: API testing fundamentals
entries.facts: API tests cover status codes, response contracts, schemas, headers, authentication, negative cases, idempotency, error handling and business rules. Validate behavior, not only HTTP 200. JSONPath extracts nested values; test isolation and environment configuration matter.

entries.title: CI/CD for test automation
entries.facts: A CI pipeline can build code, run fast unit/API checks, execute suitable UI suites, publish reports and enforce quality gates. Use secure secrets, stable test environments and clear failure diagnostics. Long end-to-end suites can run in later stages or on schedules.

entries.title: Scrum velocity
entries.facts: Velocity is the amount of work COMPLETED during a sprint, commonly counted as story points of backlog items meeting the Definition of Done. It is an observed historical measure used to forecast team capacity; it is NOT an estimation technique. It should not be used to rank teams or individuals.
must_cover: Completed work per sprint, commonly story points
Historical forecasting, not an estimation technique

entries.title: Scrum events
entries.facts: Scrum events are the Sprint, Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective. The Sprint is the container for the other events. Refinement is an ongoing activity, not a formally defined Scrum event.

entries.title: Test strategy and entry exit criteria
entries.facts: A test strategy defines scope, levels, approaches, environments, data, roles, risks, automation and reporting. Entry criteria may include build readiness and test data availability; exit criteria may include agreed coverage, acceptable defect risk and stakeholder sign-off. Criteria are tailored, not universal.

entries.title: Critical defect before release
entries.facts: For a release-blocking defect, confirm impact and reproducibility, triage severity and priority with stakeholders, communicate risk, assess workaround and fix options, verify remediation and regression, and support an evidence-based go/no-go decision. Do not unilaterally promise release safety.
must_cover: Escalate unacceptable residual risk for go/no-go decision

entries.title: Performance testing
entries.facts: Load testing checks expected workload behavior; stress testing explores beyond expected capacity; soak testing looks for long-running degradation. Define realistic workload, throughput, latency percentiles, errors and infrastructure metrics; correlate bottlenecks across services.

entries.title: HashMap versus ConcurrentHashMap
keywords: hash map vs concurrent hash map
hash map versus concurrent hash map
entries.facts: HashMap is NOT thread-safe; it allows one null key and multiple null values. ConcurrentHashMap supports safe concurrent operations across threads and does NOT allow null keys or null values. Use HashMap for non-concurrent maps; use ConcurrentHashMap for shared maps updated or read concurrently. ConcurrentHashMap individual operations are thread-safe; compound read-modify-write sequences may require compute, merge, or other atomic methods.
must_cover: HashMap permits null key/values; ConcurrentHashMap forbids null
Single-thread versus concurrent shared use case

entries.title: Agile estimation techniques
entries.facts: Planning Poker, affinity estimation, and T-shirt sizing are relative estimation techniques; story points express relative effort/complexity/uncertainty. Estimation is different from velocity: velocity is measured AFTER completion of sprint work and used for forecasting.
must_cover: Planning Poker is an estimation technique
Velocity is a completed-work measure, not estimation

entries.title: HashMap internal working
entries.facts: HashMap uses hashing to select buckets. Keys with colliding hashes are resolved by equality checks; Java 8+ may treeify heavily populated buckets under qualifying conditions. Resizing rehashes entries across a larger table. Do not claim iteration order is guaranteed.

entries.title: API authentication and authorization testing
entries.facts: Test authentication (identity) separately from authorization (permissions). HTTP 401 indicates missing or invalid authentication credentials; 403 indicates the server understands the request but refuses it. Check expired tokens, missing scopes, role boundaries, and sensitive data exposure.

entries.title: String, StringBuilder and StringBuffer
entries.facts: String is immutable; concatenation creates new string values. StringBuilder is mutable and not synchronized, generally preferred for repeated concatenation within a thread. StringBuffer is mutable with synchronized methods, but synchronization alone does not make every compound workflow atomic. String literals may be interned in the string pool.

entries.title: API test framework architecture patterns
entries.facts: Separate test scenarios/assertions from reusable HTTP clients/request specifications, environment configuration, authentication, payload/test-data factories, and reporting. Only describe these as personal implementations if CV or supplied project evidence confirms them.
